result.summary: Fixes a potential assertion crash in the transaction orphanage when trimming candidates. When the number of peers announcing orphans exceeds the global latency limit of 3,000, integer division reduced the per-peer latency score allowance to zero, causing an assertion failure in GetDosScore. The PR floors the per-peer latency share at one during eviction and adjusts candidate filtering to select peers with scores of one or higher.
result.problem: Nodes running on Linux with custom configurations permitting over 3,000 peer connections can be crashed if enough peers announce orphan transactions, because integer division floors the per-peer latency share to zero and triggers an assertion abort.

resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp reproduced the abort and pointed out that both clamping and changing the filter to >= are required to avoid an empty heap segfault.
brunoerg suggested updating the fuzz target txorphanage_sim to reach the zero-share path.
danielabrozzoni requested adding SanityCheck() calls in unit tests and clarifying eviction documentation in txorphanage.h.
